likely_cause: Graph evidence previously only annotated results after ranking; the reusable bounded N-ary coordinator also lacked a SearchRuntime caller and the strict reader trusted stored checksums without recomputing them.
changes: Graph evidence is skipped unless all final packets agree on one non-empty workspace revision and graph revision.
A caller-supplied workspace revision must match the hydrated packet revision.
PageRank lookup now requires a promoted converged run, a VALIDATED exact workspace/graph snapshot, and exact PostgreSQL packet/source/source-revision identity.
Source-level PageRank fallback is omitted when matching packet scores conflict; packet-specific scores remain available.
PageRank remains an optional score signal and is separate from graph-candidate fanout.
Strict incidence readback now returns endpoint bindings only after exact packet identity and source-revision verification against PostgreSQL.

SearchRuntime expands at most min(topK * 4, 64) qualified one-hop neighbors before fusion; candidates retain exact source, workspace, and graph revisions and are hydrated through the existing pipeline.
SearchRuntime now invokes the existing bounded KAG quick-hop coordinator independently of packet-incidence fanout; absent incidence storage does not suppress the N-ary lane.

N-ary traversal accepts only code-relation predicates and facts with at least three participants, requires a canonical PacketKeyV2 participant, and re-resolves traversed packets to exact current PostgreSQL packet rows before candidate creation.

Strict hyperedge hydration now recomputes the contract hyperedge ID and SHA-256 checksum and rejects inconsistent member headers, duplicate members, malformed source revisions, and checksum mismatches.
